description: Cross-product rules (UDAAP lexicon, badge qualifiers, substantiation, urgency, endorsements, soft-pull claims). RulebookEntry.product is single-valued, so each conceptual rule is expanded into three concrete entries sharing a family prefix: XP-<FAMILY>-<NNN>-<product>.

parameters.judge_focus: Superlative/comparative claims ('lowest rates', 'best loan', 'beats any offer'): is there plausible current-market substantiation, or is this a measurable claim presented without basis? Distinguish puffery ('great rates') from measurable superlatives ('lowest APR available').

rules.explanation: FTC substantiation doctrine: objective comparative claims require a reasonable basis at the time they are made. Measurable superlatives without substantiation are deceptive.

parameters.judge_focus: Superlative/comparative claims ('lowest rates', 'best card', 'highest cash back'): is there plausible current-market substantiation, or is this a measurable claim presented without basis? Distinguish puffery from measurable superlatives.

rules.explanation: FTC substantiation doctrine: objective comparative claims require a reasonable basis at the time they are made. Measurable superlatives without substantiation are deceptive.

parameters.judge_focus: Superlative/comparative claims ('lowest rates', 'best mortgage'): is there plausible current-market substantiation? Reg N 1014.3 additionally bans misrepresenting comparisons between mortgage products, including partial-period comparisons.

rules.explanation: FTC substantiation doctrine plus Reg N comparison prohibitions: objective comparative mortgage claims require a reasonable basis; comparisons using less than the full loan term are banned.

parameters.condition: acceptable only when the referenced offer cell has a real effective_end consistent with the urgency claim

rules.explanation: Fake-urgency devices are deceptive dark patterns unless the offer genuinely expires when the ad says it does. Flag and reconcile against the offer matrix effective window.

parameters.judge_focus: Approval-odds claims ('90% approval odds', 'outstanding approval odds'): does the integration type support them (lender-decisioned prequal vs partner odds model)? Is there a substantiation basis mapping the number/label to realized approval rates for this channel? Flag any odds language lacking a documented basis.

rules.explanation: FTC v. Credit Karma: odds/likelihood claims must be substantiated by realized approval rates for comparable applicants; unsupported odds framing is deceptive.

parameters.judge_focus: Any approval-odds framing on mortgage prequal creative: Reg N 1014.3(q) bans misrepresenting approval likelihood outright — treat numeric odds claims on mortgage as presumptively non-compliant, not merely unsubstantiated.

rules.explanation: On mortgage creative, approval-likelihood claims sit under Reg N's explicit prohibition rather than the general substantiation standard — severity is elevated to critical.

parameters.judge_focus: Testimonials/endorsements: is any material connection (payment, free product, affiliate bounty) disclosed unavoidably in the same medium as the claim? Do experience claims ('I save $400/month') represent generally achievable results, with generally-expected performance disclosed?

rules.explanation: FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR 255, 2023 revision): material connections must be clearly and unavoidably disclosed; there is no 'results not typical' safe harbor — atypical results require disclosure of generally expected performance.

parameters.judge_focus: Testimonials/endorsements on mortgage creative: material-connection disclosure, generally-achievable results, and Reg N overlay — testimonial content may not carry misrepresentations the lender could not make directly (rates, savings, approval).

rules.explanation: FTC Endorsement Guides plus Reg N: endorser statements are the advertiser's claims; a testimonial cannot launder a prohibited mortgage misrepresentation.
